assessment.nobel_worthiness: Estimating demand for differentiated products with market-level data, together with dynamic industry models, changed empirical IO. The methods are used well beyond IO, in trade, merger analysis, antitrust and public policy, and they connect structural theory to data.
assessment.attribution: The BLP framework (Berry 1994; Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes 1995) is the core contribution, and Pakes has a separate line of work on dynamic industry models. A trio of Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes is coherent. Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin contributed to related strands but are less central to this discovery. Excluding them is a real judgement call.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of use, wide adoption in competition authorities and in teaching, and robust follow-up methodological work all point to a mature contribution.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer a broader empirical-IO prize that includes Bresnahan and Reiss.
I am closest to this field, so my own familiarity may bias my assessment.
The balance of credit between the demand-estimation and dynamic-games strands is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Trade models with heterogeneous firms and selection into exporting reshaped how economists think about the gains from trade, reallocation and the margins of adjustment. They link closely to a very large body of firm-level empirical work.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the clear central contribution, and Helpman's wider work on trade with imperfect competition and firm heterogeneity (including Helpman, Melitz and Yeaple 2004) is substantial. Redding's contributions are valuable but more quantitative and spatial, so I would leave him out of the core attribution. The Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum empirical strand is not credited here and is a real attribution question.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of confirmation in theory and in firm-level data, and the framework is standard in graduate teaching.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees trade as already well served by the Krugman prize, and whether this would be too close to the new-trade-theory award.
Whether Bernard, Eaton, Jensen or Kortum should share credit.
Helpman also appears on another ballot entry, which complicates how the trade fields are compared.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fairness, reciprocity and inequity aversion explain behaviour in bargaining, public goods games, labour markets and contract incentives that standard self-interest models cannot. The work has shaped contract theory, experimental economics and policy design.
assessment.attribution: Fehr and Schmidt's 1999 model and the Fehr-Gächter experimental work are central, and Falk adds field evidence and a preference-measurement agenda. Rabin's earlier fairness theory and Bolton and Ockenfels's ERC model are close competitors for credit and are not on this ballot entry.
assessment.maturity: Core results are over twenty years old and replicated widely, although some of the experimental findings are context-dependent.
uncertainties: Priority and credit relative to Rabin, Bolton and Ockenfels, and others.
How well lab results generalize to field settings.
Whether the committee prefers to recognize behavioural economics through a different combination of laureates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Credible measurement of adverse selection and moral hazard in insurance markets, combined with welfare analysis, connects the Akerlof-Rothschild-Stiglitz theory to data. It informs health insurance design and regulation.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein and Einav are the central names for the empirical welfare approach to selection markets. Salanie contributed important econometric and theoretical work, including on insurance, and might be considered. Chiappori and Salanie's tests for asymmetric information are an earlier related contribution.
assessment.maturity: The core empirical papers date from about 2010 onward, so this is reasonably established, but the programme is younger than the other top candidates and still maturing.
uncertainties: Whether the programme is mature enough for an award.
Whether the credit should include Chiappori and Salanie's earlier tests.
Whether the field overlaps too much with the health economics category.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Formal models and empirical evidence on how electoral rules, constitutions and state capacity shape fiscal policy and economic outcomes created modern political economics. The work links theory with comparative evidence.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini's joint work on political economics and constitutions is the foundation. Besley's work on state capacity, accountability and political selection is closely linked. The 2024 prize on institutions overlaps in theme and may affect timing.
assessment.maturity: Contributions span roughly three decades, with robust follow-up literatures.
uncertainties: Possible thematic overlap with the 2024 institutions prize.
Persson's past committee service is a disclosed conflict that I do not adjudicate.
Whether the committee would prefer a narrower, more clearly defined discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data transformed the measurement of intergenerational mobility and its local determinants, and the research made large-scale causal evidence on neighbourhood effects and policy possible. It has influenced debate and policy.
assessment.attribution: Chetty leads the programme, with Hendren and Friedman as the closest collaborators on mobility and neighbourhood effects. Katz's earlier Moving to Opportunity work is an important input. Because the work is highly collaborative, individual credit is hard to separate.
assessment.maturity: Much of the work dates from the 2010s and later, so it is relatively recent, and some findings are still being tested by replication and follow-up on causal interpretation.
uncertainties: Relatively early for a prize.
Causal interpretation of place effects and replication.
How to split credit across a large team.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities, staggered price setting and the New Keynesian framework underpin modern monetary policy analysis and central bank practice. The price-adjustment microfoundations are also relevant to evidence from firm-level price-setting studies.
assessment.attribution: Calvo (staggered pricing), Taylor (staggered contracts and the policy rule) and Woodford (the integrated framework) are the most defensible three. Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets and others are strongly credited, and the three-laureate cap makes attribution contested.
assessment.maturity: Decades of use, and the framework is standard in central banks, though the 2008 crisis and the 2021-22 inflation episode raised questions about its limits.
uncertainties: Large and diffuse set of credited contributors, and the cap makes any choice contestable.
Empirical challenges to Calvo-style pricing from micro price data.
Whether the committee views the field as already rewarded through earlier macroeconomics prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and the China-shock evidence changed how economists and policymakers understand labour demand, wage inequality and the local costs of trade and automation.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to both the task-based and the trade-shock strands, with Dorn and Hanson as close co-authors on the China shock. Acemoglu's task framework has already been recognized in the 2024 prize, which affects how this entry is assessed. Katz is credited on the ballot entry, but I would not select him as part of the core trio.
assessment.maturity: Key papers date from the 2000s and 2010s. The evidence base is large, but interpretation of long-run effects is still debated.
uncertainties: Overlap with technology and inequality themes in recent prizes.
Persistence and interpretation of the China-shock effects.
How credit is divided between the technology and trade strands.
